Imagine my excitement - to finally get a good look around the Mortuga Submarine! I was even given a tour by one of Mortuga's subordinates, a Mr Godrik Gripp.
We begun by visiting a bizarre laboratory known as the 'Dream Chamber.' It smelled of dried herbs and dusty glass, but was devoid of its Dream Custodian.
Mr Gripp took me down to the cargo hold. It smells of damp wood and tarred rope. Yes, I describe it in the present tense, for it is here I sit as I write this very diary.
Next door, the engine room; burnished bronze and tea-stained parchment. I learned that it's something of a nest for Mr Gripp himself, and thus was currently unoccupied.
Outside, I encountered a Dr Zacharius Zephyr, the aforementioned keeper of the Dream Chamber. Surprised to see us, he nearly dropped the empty glass bottle he was carrying.
Clearly wishing to remove himself from the situation, the good doctor muttered something inaudible and disappeared up the ladder.
We continued on into the next room, which I was amused to discover was some kind of shimmering mermaid grotto.
I smelled her before I saw her - the unmistakeable mix of salt, seaweed and sequinned spandex. It can only be Madam Tadpole, a name which may be familiar to longtime readers of this diary.
Tadpole and I caught up while Mr Gripp skulked in the doorway, clearly hoping this would mark the end of the tour. But it did not, dear reader, it did not!!
An early disappointment - the Captain's Cabin was locked. Mr Gripp explained how Captain Mortuga mostly keeps this room locked when it's not in use.
We climbed down into the living quarters, where a pair of bunk rooms sat at the end of a corridor.
The first smelled of crayon dust and unwatered flowers. A young woman was laying in her bed, poring over an old document.
She hastily hid the document away and introduced herself as Miss Sinthia Seafoam. A name to remember, dear reader, as she will shortly become quite important.
The second bunk room smelled of aftershave and desperation. The two men within (Mr James Wirman and Mr Dirk Dansom) both appeared to be asleep - so we decided not to intrude.
Next on the tour - a room inhabited (by the looks of things) by a young child who is also a stage magician. Sadly, this mythical child-magician is nowhere to be seen.
The room at the very end of the hallway was sealed with a heavy bulkhead door. Mr Gripp dismissed it as a store room that only Captain Mortuga makes use of.
(Perhaps you'll agree with me, dear reader, when I suggest the peculiarity of a simple 'store room' being sealed off with such a significant door)
